transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's good to meet you too. 

I guess I came in because... well, I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've failed. I feel like I've failed as a father, and really just as a useful person in general. It just keeps looping in my head, over and over. It gets to the point where I start to feel like I don't really deserve much of a future.
Have you been having thoughts of killing yourself?

Well... yes. I've been having thoughts that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And... it actually scared me recently. I caught myself going over all my finances, and I realized I was doing it like I was getting things ready for someone else to take over. So, yes, the thoughts are there.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event?
Yeah... I suppose they did. This has all been going on for about a month now, ever since my daughter left for college out of state.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this?
No... no, I haven't. I mean, I've had stressful times or bad days before, just like anyone else, but never anything like this. This past month is really the first time I've ever felt this low.
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to get through your usual day-to-day responsibilities?

Yes, they have. My bills and house projects are just piling up right now because I can't seem to make myself follow through on anything. I've also stopped seeing the few people I used to count on... I don't go to my book club or out on rides anymore. I just don't feel safe brushing this off anymore, you know? Especially after I started organizing my finances like someone else might need to take them over. It's definitely getting in the way of my normal life.
Aside from thoughts about your daughter leaving for college, do you feel depressed most of the day?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean... I haven't really thought about it like that. I don't know if it's most of the day or just when she crosses my mind. It all just kind of blends together at this point.
Even when you are not thinking about your daughter leaving, do you still feel down?

I guess I don't really know. Like I said, it's hard to separate it all out. I'm just... I'm down a lot right now, but I couldn't tell you if it's always because of her or if it's just there anyway. I haven't been paying attention to it like that.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I definitely have. I used to really look forward to working on my model railway, or catching the Cubs games with my daughter. But now... the trains are just sitting there half-built on the table. I haven't touched them in a while. And even just putting a game on the TV feels completely pointless. I just don't get anything out of it anymore.
Do you feel depressed even when your daughter is not on your mind?

I mean... like I mentioned before, I really couldn't tell you. It's just hard to untangle it all. I feel down a lot, but whether she's on my mind at that exact second or not... I honestly haven't been keeping track of it like that. It just feels like a heavy cloud is there most of the time.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you would expect from your daughter leaving for college?

I honestly don't know. I mean, I've never had a child leave for college before, so I don't really have anything to compare it to. I don't know what I'm supposed to be feeling. It's... it's very overwhelming for me right now, but I couldn't tell you if it's stronger than what's expected. I just know it's a lot to deal with.
Have there been times this past month when you felt depressed even though you were not thinking about your daughter leaving for college?

Like I said, I really can't say for sure. I just... I haven't been paying attention to whether I'm actively thinking about her leaving when I feel this way. It's just a constant feeling, you know? It's just there.
Do you feel worthless?

Yes. Honestly, that's a big part of why I came in to see you. I just... I can't shake this feeling that I've completely failed. Failed as a father, and just as a useful person in general. It keeps looping in my head, over and over, until I start feeling like I really don't deserve much of a future. So, yeah, I do.
Do these feelings seem out of proportion to your daughter leaving for college?

I think... like I was saying just a minute ago, I really don't know what the normal proportion is supposed to be. I've never gone through this before. It feels huge to me, but I don't have a baseline to compare it to. So I just can't say for sure if it's out of proportion or not.
In the past month, have you felt down even during moments when your daughter was not on your mind?

I think... well, that's pretty much what you asked a couple of minutes ago. And, like I said, I really just don't know. I haven't been keeping track of exactly what I'm thinking about at any given moment. The feeling is just always there, so I can't really separate it out like that.
Do you feel hopeless?
I wouldn't say I feel hopeless, exactly. I mean, I'm not sure. I haven't really thought about it in those terms. I just feel like I'm stuck in this rut, but I don't know if I'd use the word hopeless.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Yeah, I have. Most days I just don't bother making a real meal anymore. I usually... I just forget to eat until it gets pretty late. And even then, I only manage to have some toast or a bowl of cereal. I've actually had to tighten my belt a notch or two lately, so I guess I'm losing weight from it.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, I have. It's actually been really frustrating. I mean, I used to manage complex engineering spreadsheets without even thinking about it. But lately... I'll just sit and stare at a simple grocery list, or a bill, for half an hour. And even after all that time, I still can't decide what to do next. It's like my brain just can't process it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, sleep has been a real issue. I'll just lie in bed for hours... the house is just too quiet at night, you know? And then, when I finally do manage to drift off, I almost always end up waking up around three or four in the morning. Once I'm awake, I can't get back to sleep. My mind just starts running through everything I've messed up, and I just lie there staring at the ceiling.
Do these depressed feelings happen even when you are not thinking about your daughter leaving for college?

I... I'm not sure what you mean. I don't have a daughter leaving for college. I think you might have me confused with someone else. 

But as for the feelings... yeah, they happen all the time. It doesn't really matter what I'm thinking about or what I'm doing. The heaviness is just always there.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?
I don't think so. I haven't really noticed anything like that, and no one else has mentioned it to me either. I feel like I'm moving and talking about the same as I usually do.
